title: lightweight-capture-and-safe-escalation-factory
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: On large on-call handoffs we repeatedly create ad-hoc diagnostic bundles and escalation cards; the process is error-prone and heavy. This PR introduces a lightweight capture surface plus a safe escalation factory that makes ephemeral diagnostic runs trivial for responders while enforcing redaction, rate limits, and safety gates. Goals: (1) Allow responders to assemble compact evidence bundles (logs, small trace slices, recent metrics) in <30s; (2) Provide templated escalation cards with enforced least-privilege links and auto-attach of the compact bundle; (3) Ensure automated captures run through preflight checks (quota, PII redaction rules, command safety) and staged execution with escape hatches. High level changes: new capture API endpoint /v1/oncall/capture-lite, a small UI action in the Slack responder modal, an orchestration worker that runs staged capture steps (probe -> bundle -> scrub -> attach), and an escalation factory that templates severity, owners, and recommended steps. Implementation notes: capture-lite uses existing telemetry samplers but restricts retention to 24h by default and enforces sample-size caps per-hour; scrub step runs the redaction engine with an added whitelist for trace IDs and masks AWS ARNs and IPs by default. The escalation factory is a composable template engine that serializes into the incident card JSON and links the bundle via a signed short-lived URL (HMAC, 10m TTL). Safety: preflight validators refuse captures when account quota exhausted, when CI-linked incidents are marked as sensitive, or when probe commands exceed the safe-command whitelist. The staged runner supports a dry-run mode that executes all validation and simulates capture without exporting artifacts. Backwards compatibility: existing long-form capture and evidence attachments are untouched; capture-lite is opt-in behind flag incident.capture_lite_enabled. Checklist: - [x] API surface and schema agreed in design doc ENG-8721 - [x] Unit tests for scrub rules and quota checks - [x] End-to-end test exercising Slack modal flow (simulated tokens) - [x] Canary rollout to 10% of on-call groups - [x] Docs update for responder runbooks (doc link attached) Testing performed: local and CI unit tests, integration test using the telemetry sandbox with synthetic traces, an internal canary run across two teams, and a security review focusing on redaction logic. Rollout plan: feature flag gated, 10% -> 50% -> 100% with metric monitoring on capture rate, bundle size, and failed-redaction alerts. Related: SUP-1099 (customer request for faster capture during escalations), ENG-8799 (follow-up to add automated remediation hints).
